Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — RetailEdge is excited to move from eval to procurement. Per my conversation with Finance, they need a concise MAP that ties technical acceptance to procurement milestones (PO issuance, billing routing, invoice cadence). Can you send a short mutual action plan and the draft PO language for the GCP private offer?

Key constraints from our side:
- Technical acceptance window: 10 business days once we get a staging image and test prompts loaded.
- Billing: we prefer Marketplace invoicing to flow to our central AP team (Net 45).

Subject: Joint Acceptance Roadmap & GCP private offer — RetailEdge (draft MAP + PO)

Samira — thanks for the clear asks. Draft MAP and PO language attached (RetailEdge_MAP_v1.xlsx, RetailEdge_GCP_PO_Draft.pdf). High-level plan below; I put owner and ETA per step so Finance can see the gating sequence.

1) Technical prep (owner: RetailEdge / Redwood engineering) — start: day 0, ETA: 3 business days
   - We provide a staging endpoint and short runbook for loading test prompts.
   - Acceptance criteria: 1) response latency within agreed SLO on peak test profile; 2) output quality per the shared eval set (>= baseline).

2) Technical acceptance signoff (owner: RetailEdge technical contact: Oliver) — ETA: day 10
   - Oliver signs off on the acceptance sheet (attached tab in MAP).

3) Marketplace private offer activation (owner: Jonas / Redwood marketplace ops) — parallel to signoff; ETA: day 5–12
   - We request GCP private offer creation (SKUs + commitment). GCP requires PO and a signed ordering document; we will submit draft PO for RetailEdge to attach to their PO.

4) Procurement / PO issuance (owner: RetailEdge procurement) — ETA: day 12–20
   - RetailEdge issues a PO referencing the GCP private offer ID and Redwood invoice instructions. Finance indicated Net 45; please confirm billing contact for invoicing.

5) Billing activation & first invoice (owner: Redwood billing) — ETA: month boundary after activation
   - Option A: Marketplace invoicing to RetailEdge AP (preferred).
   - Option B: Direct Redwood invoice if Marketplace path blocked; requires an interim finance approval.

I've flagged two potential blockers for Finance: (a) if the private offer cannot route invoices to RetailEdge AP directly (GCP sometimes requires reseller routing), and (b) if legal redlines require modifications to our standard ordering terms. Both are shown in the MAP with contingency steps.

Next steps:
- Kimberly: can you confirm expected invoice recipient email and whether RetailEdge's tax form was already shared?
- Marissa: can you confirm standard timeframe for private-offer activation with GCP from our side?

I'll follow up with GCP Marketplace support after we get a confirmation from RetailEdge on invoice routing.

Thanks — Jonas
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
